name: Milieudefensie and Others v Royal Dutch Shell

jurisdiction.court: Rechtbank Den Haag (The Hague District Court, first instance) and Gerechtshof Den Haag (The Hague Court of Appeal, appeal)

description: Civil action brought by the NGO Milieudefensie (Friends of the Earth Netherlands) and other organisations against Royal Dutch Shell, with more than 17,000 co-claimants, seeking an order to reduce the group’s CO2 emissions (Scope 1, 2 and 3) by 45% by 2030 compared with 2019 levels, on the basis of the duty of care (Art. 6:162 BW), the Paris Convention and Arts 2 and 8 ECHR.
outcome: At first instance (2021) The Hague District Court upheld the claim, ordering Shell to reduce emissions by 45% by 2030: the first judgment in the world to impose a reduction obligation on a private company. On appeal (12 November 2024) the Court recognised that Shell has an obligation to reduce its emissions based on the duty of care, but held that a specific reduction percentage could not be imposed on it; it therefore set aside the first-instance judgment and dismissed all of Milieudefensie’s claims, ordering it to pay the costs. A leading precedent for corporate climate litigation.
